questions.question: A student wants to increase the magnetic strength of an electromagnet. What modification to the coil of wire will achieve this?
options: Using fewer turns of wire in the coil
Increasing the number of turns of wire in the coil
Using a shorter piece of wire with the same number of turns
Unwinding the wire so it is no longer a coil

questions.question: How does changing the electric current flowing through an electromagnet's coil affect its magnetic field?
options: Increasing the current makes the magnetic field stronger.
Decreasing the current makes the magnetic field stronger.
Increasing the current reverses the magnetic poles.
Changing the current has no effect on the strength of the magnetic field.

questions.question: Why will an electromagnet made from bare, uninsulated copper wire fail to function if the adjacent turns of the coil are touching each other?
options: The current bypasses the loops of the coil, short-circuiting them.
The magnetic field lines from touching loops cancel each other out completely.
The bare wire cannot conduct electricity when in contact with itself.
Touching wire turns causes the iron core to melt due to high resistance.

questions.question: Why does placing a soft iron core inside the coil of an electromagnet make the magnet much stronger?
options: The iron core conducts the electric current directly into the object being attracted.
The iron core cools the wire, allowing more current to flow.
The iron core becomes magnetised when the current is turned on.
The iron core permanently retains its magnetism to double the field strength.

questions.question: What physical phenomenon occurs in the space immediately surrounding a straight wire when an electric current passes through it?
options: A magnetic field is created around the wire.
The air around the wire becomes permanently magnetised.
The wire starts to repel all nearby copper objects.
The magnetic poles of the wire swap places constantly.

questions.question: Why is the magnetic field of a coiled wire (solenoid) much stronger than that of a single straight wire carrying the same current?
options: The coil prevents heat from escaping, which multiplies the magnetic force.
The magnetic fields of the individual loops add together to create a stronger combined field.
Coiling the wire converts electrical current into permanent static magnetism.
The electric current travels faster through a coiled wire than a straight wire.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent bar magnet?
options: It does not require any magnetic poles to function.
It can be turned on and off using an electric current.
It is permanently magnetic and never loses its strength over time.
It only attracts non-metallic materials like wood and plastic.

questions.question: If you bring the north-seeking pole of one bar magnet close to the north-seeking pole of another bar magnet, what will happen?
options: The two poles will attract each other.
The two poles will repel each other.
The poles will spin around to find a south pole.
There will be no force between them at all.

questions.question: How does a piece of unmagnetised magnetic material, like iron, behave when placed near the poles of a bar magnet?
options: It is attracted to the north-seeking pole but repelled by the south-seeking pole.
It is repelled by both the north-seeking and south-seeking poles.
It is attracted to both the north-seeking and south-seeking poles.
It is only affected by the south-seeking pole.

questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only the three metallic elements that are magnetic?
options: Iron, copper, and aluminium
Iron, cobalt, and nickel
Gold, silver, and copper
Nickel, zinc, and tin

questions.question: Why does the north-seeking pole of a freely suspended bar magnet point towards the Earth's geographic North Pole?
options: The Earth behaves as if it has a giant magnetic field.
The Earth's gravity pulls specifically on north-seeking magnetic poles.
The North Pole has a high concentration of permanent electrostatic charge.
The Sun's magnetic field pulls the magnet toward the north.

questions.question: How does a plotting compass behave when it is placed near a bar magnet?
options: Its needle spins continuously in circles.
Its needle lines up with the magnetic field of the magnet.
Its needle always points directly at the geometric center of the magnet.
Its needle becomes demagnetised and points randomly.

questions.question: In which direction can a magnetic field line be traced around a bar magnet?
options: From the south-seeking pole to the north-seeking pole
From the center of the magnet outwards to both poles simultaneously
From the north-seeking pole to the south-seeking pole
In circular loops that only exist inside the metal itself

questions.question: What do the arrows drawn on magnetic field lines represent?
options: The direction of the electric current flowing through the magnet
The direction of the force that would act on a north-seeking pole placed at that point
The path that a south-seeking pole would take to escape the magnetic field
The speed at which the magnetic field is radiating outward

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental rule regarding how magnetic field lines are drawn?
options: They always cross over each other at the strongest parts of the field.
They are continuous and do not cross over each other.
They start at a pole and end abruptly in empty space.
They only form straight, parallel lines that never bend.

questions.question: In an electric bell, why must the electromagnet break its own electrical circuit when it attracts the striker?
options: To prevent the battery from overheating and draining instantly
To allow the striker to spring back to its original position
To reverse the poles of the electromagnet and push the striker away
To increase the voltage for the next strike

questions.question: What causes the spinning coil of wire (electromagnet) inside an electric motor to keep rotating?
options: Other permanent magnets around the coil push it round when a current flows through it.
The electric current physically blows air against the coil to spin it.
The coil is attracted to the gravity of the motor's outer casing.
The wire coil constantly expands and contracts, causing it to roll.
